<result>## Verification results — PR #65, 15 claims

Methodology: read every cited file directly in the HEAD worktree, diffed against BASE (`269d5d4`) for every "new/changed" assertion, grepped the full `overrides/` tree (and, where the mechanism required it, the base `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app` tree) rather than trusting the cited scope, and checked git history/blame on the specific lines for claims 2 and 15. All line numbers below are what I read directly, not copied from the claims.

---

**1. Dead responsive-image pipeline — CONFIRMED**
`overrides/app/utils/contentfulImage.ts` defines `buildContentfulResponsiveImage`/`ContentfulResponsiveImage`/`avifSrcSet`/`webpSrcSet`. Grepping all of `overrides/app/components`, `overrides/app/utils`, `overrides/app/pages` finds zero consumers outside the function's own file and its own test (`contentfulImage.test.ts`). `megaMenuContent/index.tsx:152` and `drawer-menu/index.tsx:223` both render `<Image src={promoImage.src} ... />`, and `resolveImageEntry.ts:29` shows `promoImage.src` is literally `asset.fields.file.url` — the raw Contentful asset URL with no query string at all. The pipeline is fully dead code today.

**2. Mega-menu stuck-open edge case — CONFIRMED**, with an important refinement.
Traced the full path: `useMegaMenuMotion.ts`'s `CLOSE` case for `phase === 'expanding'` (lines 65-67) jumps straight to `'collapsing'`. In `list-menu-popover.tsx`, `useTransitionSafeValue` (lines 38-57) defers the real `setValue` by two `requestAnimationFrame`s. If `CLOSE` lands before that double-rAF resolves, `value` is still at its pre-HOVER default ('0fr'), the new target recomputed for `'collapsing'` is *also* `'0fr'` — so the DOM's `grid-template-rows` never actually changes, no CSS transition fires, `onTransitionEnd` never fires, `onCollapseComplete` is never dispatched, and the reducer never reaches `COLLAPSE_COMPLETE` — `activeItemId` stays non-null forever. I confirmed the visible symptom too: `header/index.tsx:160-169`'s `isMegaMenuOpen` is driven only by `list-menu.tsx:59-65`'s `activeItemId`-gated effect, and `rightBar/index.tsx:175-185` renders the "Close" text+X control whenever `menuExpanded === 'fullSwap'` (i.e., `isMegaMenuOpen`) — so the described end state (Close control shown, panel invisible) is real. Notably, `git show 13ce33e` shows the *exact* `CLOSE`-during-`'expanding'`→`'collapsing'` code path was added by a prior CodeRabbit-fix commit for a *related but different* bug (the opacity/content-fade side of the same problem) — that fix correctly handles content-fade but has no visibility into `useTransitionSafeValue`'s separate double-rAF deferral, so this height-side gap survived it.
Refinement: `useMegaMenuMotion.test.ts` has **13** `test()` blocks, not 14 (verified by count and by reading the whole file) — minor factual correction, doesn't affect the substance. All 13 operate via `renderHook`+reducer only, confirmed. I also checked `list-menu-popover.test.tsx`, which the original finding didn't cite — it *does* test CSS/rAF behavior (including the double-rAF deferral itself, lines 265-270), but every case renders a single static `motionPhase` prop; none rerenders from `'expanding'` to `'collapsing'` within the same test, so it doesn't hit this interleaving either. No test at any layer exercises it.

**3. useHeaderNav fetch-failure doc/behavior mismatch — CONFIRMED**
`useHeaderNav.ts:46` doc: `` `items` is `undefined` while loading, on fetch failure, or when no entry resolves``. Implementation, lines 78-82: `isLoading ? undefined : resolved ? filterByRegion(...) : []`. On error, `useQuery` settles `isLoading=false` with `data` still `undefined`, so `resolved` is `undefined` and `items` resolves to `[]`, not `undefined`. Grepped all non-test files in `overrides/app` for `isError`: only `useHeaderNav.ts` (defines/returns it) and `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (unrelated `isProductError`/`isCategoryError`). `list-menu.tsx` and `drawer-menu/index.tsx` read neither.

**4. Stale "not wired" doc comments — CONFIRMED**
`headerTypes.ts:17-21` and `leftBar/index.tsx:18-19,22` and `rightBar/index.tsx:79-80,84` all state the values are "not wired to any real mega-menu/drawer state on this branch." `header/index.tsx:160-203` demonstrably wires real state: `isMegaMenuOpen`/`MegaMenuOpenContext` (fed by `list-menu.tsx`'s `activeItemId` via `useMegaMenuOpenReporter`) and `useHeaderMenuExpandedState`, combined into `menuExpanded`/`onCloseMenu` and passed at `header/index.tsx:231` (`<LeftBar ... menuExpanded={menuExpanded} onBack={handleBack}>`) and `:248-249` (`<RightBar ... menuExpanded={menuExpanded} onClose={onCloseMenu} />`).

**5. Stale navGroup.js comment — CONFIRMED**
`headerNavItem.js:29-31`: "`navGroup` is authored on a separate branch ... and has no local file in this content-types/ directory yet." `scripts/contentful/content-types/navGroup.js` is a full, complete file, added by this same PR (`git diff --name-status` shows `A scripts/contentful/content-types/navGroup.js`).

**6. list-menu barrel misexport — CONFIRMED**
`overrides/app/components/list-menu/index.ts` doesn't exist at base (`ls` fails on the base worktree). Line 3: `export { ListMenuPopover } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/list-menu/list-menu-popover';` — the base path. The local override `list-menu-popover.tsx` is 282 lines vs. base's 80, and is substantively different (full motion-phase integration, keyboard nav, `useTransitionSafeValue`). Exhaustive grep of every `ListMenuPopover` reference in `overrides/` (including tests/stories) shows the real consumer, `list-menu.tsx:3`, and the test file `list-menu-popover.test.tsx:7`, both import directly from `'./list-menu-popover'`, bypassing the barrel entirely — so the bug is currently latent (no live consumer hits it) but is a real, confirmed defect in the barrel's source.

**7. Missing `_focusVisible` on several new IconButtons — CONFIRMED**
Grepped `leftBar/index.tsx` and `rightBar/index.tsx` in full for `_focusVisible`: zero matches in either file, confirming none of the 6 cited IconButtons (leftBar hamburger `:83`; rightBar tablet search `:205`, account trigger `:242`, mobile search `:387`, mobile bag `:427`, mobileL2 close `:452`) sets it. Contrast confirmed: `zimmNavItem.css.ts:47-51` (`light` variant) and `:55-59` (`inverse` variant) set it explicitly; `zimmSearchInput/index.tsx:103-106` (the clear button, a direct Chakra prop, not in `zimmSearchInput.css.ts` — worth noting since the claim didn't name the file) sets it explicitly; `header.css.ts:73-74` (`logoButton` part) sets it explicitly (`_focusVisible: { outline: 0 }`, paired with `_focus: { boxShadow: 'outline' }`).

**8. Nested `<nav>` landmark regression — CONFIRMED**
`leftBar/index.tsx:99`: `<chakra.nav __css={styles.nav}>{children}</chakra.nav>`. `children` resolves to `<ListMenu>` at tablet+ (via `header/index.tsx:231-233` forwarding Header's own `children`, which base `_app/index.jsx` sets to `<ListMenu>`), and `list-menu.tsx:77` renders `<nav id="list-menu" aria-label="Main navigation" ...>` as `ListMenuView`'s own root — a `<nav>` nested inside a `<nav>`, the outer one carrying no `aria-label` at all. Base-commit comparison: `git show 269d5d4:overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx` line 236 shows the old header wrapped `{children}` in `<Box {...styles.bodyContainer}>{children}</Box>` — a plain `Box`, not a `nav`. This is a genuine new regression introduced by this PR's LeftBar/RightBar split.

**9. PopoverFooter onClick on non-interactive element — CONFIRMED** (structure), independent risk read: **low-impact, not a keyboard trap**.
`rightBar/index.tsx:304`: `<PopoverFooter onClick={handleSignout} cursor={...}>`, inner `<Button variant="unstyled" {...headerStyles.signout} isDisabled={isSigningOut}>` at `:306` with no `onClick` of its own. Confirmed at the library level: `node_modules/@chakra-ui/popover/dist/popover-footer.js:42-52` shows `PopoverFooter` is literally `chakra.footer` with `...props` spread — no role, no keyboard handling added. My own assessment: this is *not* a keyboard trap — Chakra's `Button` renders a real native `<button>`, so Enter/Space while it's focused produces a genuine `click` DOM event that bubbles to the ancestor `<footer onClick>` exactly like a mouse click, so keyboard activation works correctly today. The real (minor) defect is scope creep — clicking anywhere in the footer's padding/Divider area, not just the button, also triggers sign-out — a code-smell/maintainability risk (fragile if the child ever stops being a native interactive element) rather than a live a11y bug.

**10. `/login` duplicated literal — CONFIRMED**
`header/index.tsx:215` (`navigate('/login')`) and `drawer-menu/index.tsx:24` (`const SIGN_IN_HREF = '/login';`) are the only two files in `overrides/app` containing the literal `'/login'` (grep confirmed, tests/stories excluded). `overrides/app/routes.tsx` exists but contains no reference to "login" at all (case-insensitive grep, zero matches) — it's a route-table file, not a constants module, so no existing shared constant was available for either site to use.

**11. SFCC-96/97 mega-menu/drawer work is separable — CONFIRMED**
`list-menu.tsx:90-122`: `itemsCount > 0 ? <ListMenuPopover .../> : <ZimmNavItem label={label} href={href} .../>` — a zero-columns item renders a plain link with zero mega-menu machinery invoked. `headerNavItem.js:32-39`: `columns` field is `required: false`, with `:28` documenting "0 columns = direct link via `href`". `drawer-menu/index.tsx:54-79` (`DrawerMenuL1Nav`) takes only `items`/`onDrillInto`/`styles` — no dependency on `activeItem`/`isDrilledIn` — and is rendered in `DrawerMenuView`'s `else` branch (`:187-190`), fully independent of L2 (`DrawerMenuL2Nav`, `:86-119`, which only renders in the sibling `isDrilledIn && activeItem` branch, `:183-186`). The footer wishlist/account/sign-in links (`:195-216`) render whenever `!isDrilledIn`, also independent of L2. Code-level separability is real and directly verified; I can't independently verify the Jira ticket-to-code mapping (which ticket literally owns which behavior) from source alone.

**12. `responsive/index.tsx` sitewide breakpoint change — CONFIRMED, and broader than the claim states.**
File is new (`ls` fails at base). Base `node_modules/.../components/responsive/index.jsx:17,31` hardcodes `lg` (this project's own `theme.breakpoints.lg = '62em'` in `gridSystem.ts:16`, i.e. 992px, unchanged from Chakra's stock default). The new override (`responsive/index.tsx:10`) sets `MOBILE_DESKTOP_SPLIT = 'md'` (`'48em'` = 768px). Grepping `overrides/app` alone for real (non-comment) JSX usage of `HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile` finds exactly **one** active consumer file: `product-view/index.tsx` (2 usages, lines 712/718/908/914) — `header/index.tsx:273`'s reference is commented out. But because this repo's `ccExtensibility` resolver redirects *every* import of `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/responsive` to this override at real-build time, not just imports from within `overrides/`, I additionally grepped the base template tree and found **9 more real, active, un-overridden consumers** that will silently inherit the new 768px split: `_app/index.jsx` (root shell), `product-item/index.jsx`, `search/index.jsx`, `search/partials/search-suggestions-section.jsx`, `bonus-product-view-modal/index.jsx`, `hooks/use-dnt-notification.js`, `pages/checkout/partials/checkout-footer.jsx`, `pages/checkout-one-click/partials/one-click-checkout-footer.jsx`, and `pages/product-list/index.jsx` (PLP). So the true blast radius (10 distinct files: PDP, PLP, product tiles, search, search-suggestions, bonus-product modal, DNT notice, both checkout footers, and the app shell) is materially larger than a naive `overrides/`-only grep would show — the claim's "app-wide, not just header/footer" framing understates rather than overstates the real scope.

**13. `globalStyles.ts` new `#app-main` rule — CONFIRMED**
`git diff` confirms pure addition: `zimmAppMain` (lines 228-238) and its registration `'#app-main': zimmAppMain` are new, no removal. `node_modules/.../components/_app/index.jsx:461-468` shows `<Box as="main" id="app-main" role="main" ...>{children}</Box>` wrapping every route's page content, positioned as a sibling between Header and Footer in the un-forked base app shell — so this rule genuinely applies grid-margin/max-width tokens to the literal main-content wrapper of every page in the app, not just header/footer.

**14. Footer/Contentful files unrelated to SFCC-52/746/747/96/97 — CONFIRMED for 3 of 4 items; UNSUPPORTED for one.**
- `footer.css.ts` (946px fix): confirmed as the tip commit (`10eb79d fix(footer): wrap site-map columns under subscribe until 946px` — matches `git log` head exactly). No evident header coupling.
- `footerConfig.js` +phoneLabel/whatsAppLabel/emailLabel: confirmed via diff. `ContactIconRow`/`zimmContactIconRow` (the consumer) has zero header call sites (grepped) — genuinely footer-only.
- Footer copy → `uiCopy`: confirmed real — `footer/index.tsx` diff shows `aria-label="Zimmermann home"` (hardcoded) replaced with `t('footer.button.assistive_msg.logo', 'Zimmermann home')`. This specific string is footer-only in effect, though it rides on a `useUiCopy.ts` mechanism extension (interpolation/`values`) that header's own new copy actually needed (`.../rightBar/index.tsx`'s `{numItems}` interpolation) — a shared-plumbing nuance, not a contradiction.
- **`footerNavGroup.js` deletion / `navGroup.js` creation — this is NOT unrelated, contrary to the claim's "none of which are required by any of the 5 header/nav tickets."** `navGroup.js:7-10` states it is "generalised from footerNavGroup so both the footer and the header mega-menu can reference the same shape," and `headerNavItem.js:38` validates its own `columns` field against `linkContentType: ['navGroup']` — the header's mega-menu literally cannot exist without `navGroup` as a content type. `footerConfig.js`'s diff independently confirms the same commit (`d934ad9 feat(contentful): unify footerNavGroup into shared navGroup type`) switched footer's own `navGroups` field from `footerNavGroup` to `navGroup` too. This is shared, load-bearing infrastructure for the header work, not a stray footer edit — the claim's blanket framing should be corrected for this one item specifically.

**15. Comment-count pattern check (4th stale-comment instance) — CONFIRMED**
`header/index.tsx:46-47`: "logoBar is capped at 114px total (desktop/tablet) ... so logo height is 66px desktop/tablet." Shipped value at `:56`: `height: {..., md: '74px', lg: '74px', xl: '74px', '2xl': '74px'}`. `git show f7d2bf2` (`fix(header): increase logo height at tablet/desktop breakpoints`, message: "66px to 74px for md and up") is a smoking-gun: it changed only the `height` value from `'66px'` to `'74px'` and left the doc comment above it completely untouched. On the "4 instances" framing: I'd flag this as worth stating precisely rather than accepting at face value — finding 4 is one conceptual scope-note propagated across 3 files (headerTypes.ts/leftBar/rightBar), finding 5 is a second, separate instance (navGroup.js), and this logo-height comment is a third. Depending whether you count finding 4 as 1 concept or 3 file-level occurrences, the total is 3 or 5, not cleanly 4 — but either way the underlying claim ("comments not updated as the branch evolved" is a real, recurring pattern, not coincidence) is well supported by direct evidence in all cases.

---

All three reviews are in and cross-verified. Here's the full picture.

## Gate table — head vs base

| Gate | Base (`269d5d4`) | Head (`10eb79d`) | Net new from this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean | none |
| `lint` | 20 problems (4E/16W), all inherited | 24 problems (5E/19W) | 1 prettier error (new `useHeaderNav.test.ts`) + 6 warnings, all in new files |
| `audit:tokens` | 4 unacknowledged (all in the old header this PR replaces) | 1 unacknowledged | net **improvement**; the 1 new hit is `footer.css.ts:20`'s `'59.125em' // 946px` — no acknowledged-exception marker |
| `test` (vitest) | 408 tests / 26 files, all passing | 612 tests / 41 files, all passing | +204 tests, all green |
| Required CI checks that actually ran | — | Branch Target ✅, Unit tests ✅, Storybook a11y ✅ all green; Playwright/BrowserStack skipped (expected, change-scoping) | |
| Mergeable | — | GitHub says CONFLICTING | only in `.claude/registry/{components,hooks}.md`, both auto-generated — trivial, not a real conflict |
| Review state | — | `REVIEW_REQUIRED`, 0 unresolved threads | CodeRabbit's "Approved ✅" late in the thread is a chat reply, not a filed approval, and it predates the current head by one commit |

Mechanically this PR is in good shape. The findings below are everything the gates can't see.

## Findings, ranked by cost of ignoring

**1. `overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx` — new override, sitewide blast radius, unrelated to any of the 5 tickets.** CONFIRMED. Changes the mobile/desktop split used by `HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile` from Chakra's default (`lg`, 992px) to `md` (768px). Because this repo's build resolver redirects *every* import of that base path, not just ones inside `overrides/`, this silently changes rendering on **10 real, active, un-overridden consumers**: the app shell itself (`_app/index.jsx`), PDP's `product-item`, PLP (`product-list/index.jsx`), `search/index.jsx` and its suggestions panel, `bonus-product-view-modal`, the DNT notice hook, and both checkout footers. None of this is reviewed, tested, or mentioned anywhere in the PR description. This is the single largest "something could quietly break on a page nobody was watching" risk in the whole diff.

**2. SFCC-747 AC10 violated — the logo is not the first focusable element.** CONFIRMED (I found this independently; zm-tester found it independently too, via the PR's *own test*, which asserts 3 Tab presses before the logo gets focus and documents in a comment that the nav/icons "sit ahead of the logoBar's logo button in DOM order"). `header/index.tsx` renders the entire nav + icon cluster before the logo in the DOM, with no `order`/`tabIndex` override anywhere in the tree to decouple tab order from visual order.

**3. SFCC-747 AC9 violated — the logo's accessible name is "Logo," never "Zimmermann."** CONFIRMED. The wrapping `<Button aria-label="Logo">` shadows the inner `<ZimmLogo aria-label="Zimmermann" role="img">` in standard accessible-name computation — a screen reader announces "Logo, button," not "Zimmermann, go to homepage."

**4. New nested `<nav>` landmark — genuine regression vs. the old header.** CONFIRMED, including the base-commit diff. `leftBar.css.ts`'s `chakra.nav` wraps `<ListMenu>`, which renders its own labeled `<nav>` — producing an unlabeled `<nav>` containing a labeled `<nav>`. The old header used a plain `<Box>` here.

**5. Mega-menu can get stuck open with a phantom "Close" control and no visible panel.** CONFIRMED via full trace (not just plausible) — a fast hover-then-close within ~2 animation frames hits a real gap between the motion reducer and its rAF-deferred value commit. Self-heals on the next hover, but no test at any layer (reducer or DOM-timing) exercises this interleaving.

**6. Mega-menu/drawer promo images ship full-resolution, unoptimized.** CONFIRMED. A complete, well-documented AVIF/WebP responsive-image builder (`contentfulImage.ts`) was built specifically for these images and has zero consumers — both actual call sites render the raw Contentful URL instead, against AGENTS.md's explicit performance rules.

**7. New `list-menu` barrel re-exports the *base* (unstyled) `ListMenuPopover`, not this PR's own 282-line override.** CONFIRMED — same defect class as the codebase's one already-known instance (`product-tile`'s `DisplayPrice`). Currently latent (the real consumer imports the override directly, bypassing the barrel), but it's exactly the kind of thing that will silently render/test wrong the next time someone imports "the normal way."

**8. Six new icon buttons omit `_focusVisible` while sibling atoms in the same PR set it explicitly.** CONFIRMED as a code inconsistency; whether it's visually broken needs a browser tab-through I can't do from here.

**Small, real cleanups (not blocking, worth a light comment):** `useHeaderNav`'s doc says fetch failure returns `undefined`; it actually always returns `[]`, and no code path reads `isError` at all. Four separate comments across this branch describe wiring or files as "not built yet" that this same PR actually completed (`headerTypes.ts`, `leftBar`/`rightBar` prop docs, `navGroup.js`'s own sibling comment in `headerNavItem.js`, and a logo-height comment claiming 66px where the shipped value is 74px) — a real, recurring pattern across a 65-commit branch, not one-off carelessness.

**Nitpicks (recorded, not for the PR):** `PopoverFooter onClick` on a non-interactive element (structurally against the rule, but the real inner `<Button>` makes this a non-issue in practice); `'/login'` typed twice with no shared constant.

## Scope verdict

**Confirmed over-scope, cleanly separable:** SFCC-96 (mega menu) and SFCC-97 (mobile drill-down, since archived into 96) are fully bundled into this PR via merged sub-branches, alongside the three you asked me to review. At the code level this is genuinely separable — a zero-`columns` nav item already renders as a plain link with no mega-menu machinery, and the mobile drawer's L1 view has zero dependency on L2 drill-down. Both absorbed tickets are Jira-assigned to Isabel Chaloner, not Tim.

**One correction to flag:** I initially had the `footerNavGroup.js` deletion filed as unrelated drive-by scope. That's wrong — verification traced it directly: the header mega-menu's content type validates against `navGroup` specifically, so unifying it with footer's type is load-bearing for SFCC-96, not a stray edit. Dropping that one. The other footer-adjacent changes (the 946px `footer.css.ts` fix, `footerConfig.js`'s new contact labels, footer copy migrating to `uiCopy`) remain genuinely unrelated to any of the 5 tickets, just small and low-risk.

**Tier 1 files — resolved, not a violation:** six files across two frozen categories are touched. I independently confirmed Tim is a real, current member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (not just self-reported) and holds repo admin, so AGENTS.md's own verified-session exception genuinely applies — this isn't unauthorized. The one loose end: the design-token change (`gridSystem.ts`/`zimmTokens.ts`) rests on an unnamed "confirmed with the design team," and I'd want that named and linked on principle, even though I separately checked the resulting numbers against the real Figma logo frame myself and they're exactly right.

## What nobody verified

Neither sub-agent has a browser, so nothing about actual rendered output, contrast ratios, or the `_focusVisible` question above was seen — only reasoned from code. I did check Figma directly myself for the logo and nav-item states (those match well), but I did not exhaustively walk all ~100 Figma nodes Marcel supplied, and I didn't visually inspect the mega-menu or mobile drawer in a live browser. Squad A/B coordination (required by `squadA.md` before touching `header/`, `footer/`, `list-menu/`, `drawer-menu/`) isn't visible from code or git history either way.

One thing worth naming: every reviewer here — including me — converged on "this is unusually well-engineered work" (extensive self-documentation, thoughtful edge-case reasoning, strong test growth). That's true, and it's exactly what makes items 2 and 3 above notable: this is polish coexisting with two missed, explicitly-worded ACs on the ticket that specifically superseded the old logo behavior to define them.

content.text:
**The two SFCC-747 violations, plain terms:**

**1. Tab order — logo should be first, but it's actually last.**
Picture using the site with a keyboard only, no mouse (this is how screen-reader users and many people with motor disabilities browse). You'd expect hitting Tab once to land on the logo, since it's the "take me home" element and the ticket explicitly requires it be first. Instead, right now, Tab takes you through the hamburger button, then all the nav links (New, Clothing, Accessories...), then Search, Account, Wishlist, and Bag — and only after all of that do you reach the logo. The PR's own test literally checks this and expects it: it does `Tab, Tab, Tab` and only then expects the logo to have focus.

Why did this happen despite the layout looking correct? The logo genuinely does sit visually below the nav bar (that part's right, and required). But browsers tab through elements in the order they appear in the *code*, not the order they appear on screen — and in the code, the developer wrote the nav bar first and the logo second. Nobody added the (fairly standard) trick to make it appear later but tab first.

**2. Accessible name — screen readers announce "Logo," not "Zimmermann."**
Screen readers read out a label for every button so a blind user knows what it does. The ticket says this one should announce "Zimmermann, go to homepage." There are actually two labels stacked here: an inner one on the logo graphic itself saying "Zimmermann," and an outer one on the button wrapping it saying just "Logo." When a button has its own label, screen readers use *only* that one and ignore anything inside it — so the "Zimmermann" label never gets heard at all. A screen reader user just hears "Logo, button."

Both are small code fixes once someone's aware of them, but as written they don't match what the ticket asks for.

**The responsive.tsx change, plain terms:**

There's one shared helper component used all over the site whose only job is "show this on mobile, hide it on desktop" (or vice versa). This PR changed where that line is drawn — the cutoff moves from 992px-wide screens down to 768px-wide screens. Anything in between (a fairly normal tablet or small-laptop window) used to count as "desktop" and will now suddenly count as "mobile" instead.

That helper isn't only used in the header. I checked, and it's also used on: the product page, the search results grid, the search suggestions dropdown, the "you might also like" popup, both checkout footers, a "do not track" popup, and the outer shell that wraps the entire site. None of those are part of this PR's actual job (they're not in any of the 5 tickets), but all of them quietly change behavior the moment this merges — and nothing in the PR mentions testing that, because nobody was looking at those pages while reviewing a "rebuild the header" PR.

Concrete example: today, someone on a 900px-wide window sees the desktop checkout footer. After this merges, without anyone touching checkout code, they'd see the mobile one instead.

Happy to go deeper on either, or we can move to the verdict calls whenever you're ready.

Still here — nothing new to add since the explanation above. Take your time; whenever you've had a chance to think through the tab-order/accessible-name issues and the `responsive.tsx` blast radius, let me know how you want to call the verdict and the breakpoint-change question and I'll move to drafting the actual review comments.

content.text:
**responsive.tsx — the exact mechanism, from source:**

Old (base SFCC), hardcoded:
```js
HideOnDesktop: display={{base: 'block', lg: 'none'}}   // visible 0–991px, hidden 992px+
HideOnMobile:  display={{base: 'none', lg: 'block'}}   // hidden 0–991px, visible 992px+
```
New (this PR):
```ts
const MOBILE_DESKTOP_SPLIT = 'md';  // was 'lg'
HideOnDesktop: display={{base: 'block', md: 'none'}}   // visible 0–767px, hidden 768px+
HideOnMobile:  display={{base: 'none', md: 'block'}}   // hidden 0–767px, visible 768px+
```
So concretely: at a window width of, say, 850px — under the old code that's still "mobile" (850 < 992), under the new code it's now "desktop" (850 ≥ 768). Anything using these two helpers flips which version it shows across that whole 768–991px band.

One thing I should've surfaced the first time: the developer did leave a reason, not a silent change — the code comment says the header/footer/mega-menu already switch at 768px (`md`), but this generic helper was still switching at 992px (`lg`), so in that 768–991px band, something wrapped in both helpers could end up hidden by both simultaneously — a real "dead zone" bug, not an arbitrary pick. That's a legitimate justification for *why* — it doesn't change that the 9 other pages inheriting it (PDP, PLP, search, checkout, etc.) weren't part of anyone's test plan for this PR.

**On the tab-order point — I want to push on this a bit rather than just drop it, because there's a real tension here:**

WCAG has a principle (2.4.3, "meaningful sequence") that generally says tab order *should* match visual/reading order — so nav-first-then-logo, matching what's visually on screen, is actually the *safer* default from that angle. Deliberately making the logo jump to first in tab order while staying visually second (which is what satisfying AC10 literally would require) is the kind of DOM/visual mismatch that's normally flagged as its *own* accessibility smell.

But the Jira ticket (SFCC-747, AC10) is explicit and unambiguous: *"Given a keyboard-only user is navigating the header, when they Tab to the logo, then the logo link is the first focusable element in the header, before any navigation items or icons."* I checked its full history — that's the only version of this AC that's ever existed, set once on 2026-08-14, never revised.

So: are you saying that AC is simply wrong/outdated and should be corrected in Jira (nav-first is the actual intended, correct behavior), or is there something else reconciling this I'm not seeing? I don't want to quietly drop a written, confirmed AC without your explicit call on it, but I also don't want to hold the PR to a requirement that's arguably fighting a more fundamental accessibility principle.

content.text:
They're not the same mechanism at all — and digging into this surfaced something more useful than the original question.

**Different code, no shared plumbing.** I checked: `footer.css.ts`'s 946px value has zero connection to `responsive.tsx`. It's a private constant (`BP_CONTENT_WRAP = '59.125em'`) used only in a raw CSS `@media` query inside `footer.css.ts` itself, controlling one specific thing — whether the site-map link columns sit beside the subscribe box or wrap underneath it. It never touches `HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile` or the shared `md`/`lg` breakpoint keys `responsive.tsx` uses. The footer has always had its own separate breakpoint scheme (`BP.tablet`=768px, `BP.desktop`=1024px, defined in `footerShared.ts`), independent of the generic Chakra breakpoints. So these are two unrelated "breakpoint changes" that just happen to land in the same PR.

**There's a small irony worth knowing, though.** The `responsive.tsx` change justifies moving to 768px on the logic that "768px is already the line everywhere else — header, footer, mega-menu." But this PR's own footer work is doing the opposite in the same breath: the 946px comment says 768px specifically *didn't leave enough room* for the footer's site-map columns and subscribe box to sit side by side, so it needed its own separate, wider cutoff. Same PR, same general area, two different answers to "is 768 the right line" — not a contradiction exactly, just a sign that 768px isn't some universally correct number, it's just this design system's label for "tablet."

**The actually useful thing I found chasing this down:** `footerShared.ts` still defines `BP.tabletWide` (860px), and `footer.css.ts`'s `linksInner` block still uses it (`gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-5xl)'` at that width). That exact constant, in that exact file, is what **PR #69** — a separate, already-open, already-CodeRabbit-clean PR — is actively **deleting**, with the stated reason "it was our own invention, not a design constraint, and it was making the tablet footer worse." Same file, same style block, opposite direction. Whichever of #65 or #69 merges to `develop` second is going to either fail to compile (`BP.tabletWide` no longer exists) or silently resurrect the exact thing #69 is trying to remove. That's a real, concrete coordination problem between two live PRs — worth a heads-up to whoever owns #69 before either one merges, regardless of what we decide on #65.

what does this mean for the scoped items in this PR: "responsive.tsx — the exact mechanism, from source:
Old (base SFCC), hardcoded:

```
HideOnDesktop: display={{base: 'block', lg: 'none'}}   // visible 0–991px, hidden 992px+
HideOnMobile:  display={{base: 'none', lg: 'block'}}   // hidden 0–991px, visible 992px+
```

New (this PR):

```
const MOBILE_DESKTOP_SPLIT = 'md';  // was 'lg'
HideOnDesktop: display={{base: 'block', md: 'none'}}   // visible 0–767px, hidden 768px+
HideOnMobile:  display={{base: 'none', md: 'block'}}   // hidden 0–767px, visible 768px+
```

So concretely: at a window width of, say, 850px — under the old code that's still "mobile" (850 < 992), under the new code it's now "desktop" (850 ≥ 768). Anything using these two helpers flips which version it shows across that whole 768–991px band.
One thing I should've surfaced the first time: the developer did leave a reason, not a silent change — the code comment says the header/footer/mega-menu already switch at 768px (`md`), but this generic helper was still switching at 992px (`lg`), so in that 768–991px band, something wrapped in both helpers could end up hidden by both simultaneously — a real "dead zone" bug, not an arbitrary pick. That's a legitimate justification for why — it doesn't change that the 9 other pages inheriting it (PDP, PLP, search, checkout, etc.) weren't part of anyone's test plan for this PR.
On the tab-order point — I want to push on this a bit rather than just drop it, because there's a real tension here:
WCAG has a principle (2.4.3, "meaningful sequence") that generally says tab order should match visual/reading order — so nav-first-then-logo, matching what's visually on screen, is actually the safer default from that angle. Deliberately making the logo jump to first in tab order while staying visually second (which is what satisfying AC10 literally would require) is the kind of DOM/visual mismatch that's normally flagged as its own accessibility smell.
But the Jira ticket (SFCC-747, AC10) is explicit and unambiguous: "Given a keyboard-only user is navigating the header, when they Tab to the logo, then the logo link is the first focusable element in the header, before any navigation items or icons." I checked its full history — that's the only version of this AC that's ever existed, set once on 2026-08-14, never revised.
So: are you saying that AC is simply wrong/outdated and should be corrected in Jira (nav-first is the actual intended, correct behavior), or is there something else reconciling this I'm not seeing? I don't want to quietly drop a written, confirmed AC without your explicit call on it, but I also don't want to hold the PR to a requirement that's arguably fighting a more fundamental accessibility principle." ELI5

Yes and no — there's an explanation for *what* the fix does, but nothing explaining *why it belongs in this PR*.

**What exists:** the code comment and the commit message both explain the technical reasoning — a real bug where content between 768–991px screen widths could get hidden by both the mobile and desktop versions at once. That part's genuine.

**What doesn't exist:** nowhere — not the PR's own top-level description, not Jira, not the planning doc — is there any explanation for why this ships bundled into the header PR instead of its own small fix. It's folded into one commit titled "mobile drawer full-screen rework, mega-menu polish, responsive breakpoint fix" — three unrelated things fixed together in one sitting, not a deliberate scoping call.

**And it was never actually reviewed.** CodeRabbit touched this exact file exactly once across the whole PR — but about a completely different topic (an import-style question, which Tim correctly answered). The breakpoint value itself, or its reach into 9 other pages, was never once raised in 24 rounds of review.

**One more wrinkle I just found, and it undercuts the stated reason a bit:** the commit message justifies this as fixing a bug affecting "the mobile hamburger nor desktop nav." But I checked — the header's only reference to this helper had already been commented out by Tim himself, the *day before*, in a separate commit. So by the time this fix landed, the specific header problem it describes fixing didn't actually exist anymore in the header's own code. The fix may still be correct for the other 9 pages that do use it — but the justification written for it doesn't hold up against what the header looked like at that point.

So: real bug, plausible fix, zero scoping decision behind bundling it here, and zero review of the actual change. That's the honest state of it.

content.text:
**Ticket: SFCC-747 "Logo Masthead – PWA Kit Component". Acceptance Criteria #10**, under its "Accessibility" section:

> "Given a keyboard-only user is navigating the header, when they Tab to the logo, then the logo link is the first focusable element in the header, before any navigation items or icons."

https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-747

I pulled this from the ticket's full field history, not just its current display — the Acceptance Criteria field was set exactly once, 2026-08-14, by Isabel Chaloner (the reporter), and never edited since. So this isn't a stale leftover from an earlier draft that got quietly superseded — it's the one and only version that's ever existed, sitting alongside three sibling accessibility ACs (#8 accessible name, #9 announced destination, #11 focus ring contrast) that are all still valid and all still map cleanly to real code. #10 is the odd one out among its own siblings.

Your read is a legitimate industry position — plenty of sites put a skip-link or the nav first, and WCAG's own "meaningful sequence" guidance leans that direction rather than mandating logo-first. But that's a genuine disagreement with what's written, not a misreading on my part. Given it's Isabel's own explicit, deliberate line item (not boilerplate), this reads to me as a call for whoever owns the ticket (Isabel as reporter, Dani Rivett as assignee) to actually make and record — not something to resolve silently either direction inside a code review. Want me to raise it there directly, or would you rather that conversation happen outside the PR and we just note in-thread that this AC is disputed rather than either confirming or rejecting it ourselves?
